plugins.name: wasp-nest-core
plugins.description: Start, route, document, review and govern every project.
plugins.why: The permanent foundation: setup, source knowledge, security, quality and repository gates stay available to every workflow.

plugins.name: website-audit-tools
plugins.description: Audit a public website with crawl, SEO, accessibility, conversion and evidence-backed reports.
plugins.why: A public-site engagement has its own intake, saved crawl, scoring, passive security and reporting contract.

plugins.name: code-audit-tools
plugins.description: Audit repositories and app security, measure bloat, inspect branches and plan remediation.
plugins.why: Code and owned-app investigation use source/effect evidence and stack-specific security. They must not inherit passive website permissions.

plugins.name: documentation-tools
plugins.description: Refresh, extract, publish and package documentation from real sources.
plugins.why: Advanced documentation production is optional. Basic Library and Knowledge authorship remains in core.

plugins.name: web-development-tools
plugins.description: Build web interfaces and sites with React, Svelte, design systems and accessible components.
plugins.why: Keep the interface workflow together, with stack routing inside the pack. A developer chooses one coherent web pack instead of many tiny UI packages.

plugins.name: backend-and-desktop-tools
plugins.description: Implement TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, native apps, APIs and terminal workflows.
plugins.why: Implementation languages and native delivery share code ownership and build boundaries; mobile store publication stays beside app delivery.

plugins.name: data-and-ai-tools
plugins.description: Design data, retrieval, AI runtime, model tooling and agent operations.
plugins.why: Storage, retrieval and AI orchestration form one technical journey. IDE/session tools remain opt-in; TARS retains its Claude-desktop-only prerequisite.

plugins.name: platform-and-release-tools
plugins.description: Integrate authentication, payments, analytics, messaging and production delivery.
plugins.why: The ship-and-operate journey joins provider integration and deployment, while keeping each existing actor/approval boundary.

plugins.name: growth-and-customer-tools
plugins.description: Research buyers, acquire leads, follow up, support customers and grow accounts.
plugins.why: Acquire, serve and retain is a coherent business journey. These generic methods must not acquire mandatory Littlebird or HighLevel dependencies.

plugins.name: business-and-product-tools
plugins.description: Form and run a company, discover product needs, hire teams and improve delivery.
plugins.why: Company and product decisions belong together, while legal/finance actions retain their existing explicit-request scope.

plugins.name: media-and-creative-tools
plugins.description: Create consented photography and integrate voice and video production.
plugins.why: Media has asset consent, provider job and metadata rules that should not inflate core. Ship blank model templates, never ingested people.

plugins.name: browser-and-app-testing-tools
plugins.description: Automate browsers, capture live apps and measure Lighthouse/PageSpeed behavior.
plugins.why: Browser/CDP expertise and authenticated capture are reused by audit and engineering workflows without duplicating their implementations.

plugins.name: highlevel
plugins.description: Integrate HighLevel, build with AI Studio and map exported workflows.
plugins.why: Keep the vendor-specific connection and creation workflow together; its provider/account requirements do not belong in generic growth tools.

plugins.name: littlebird-toolkit
plugins.description: Turn Littlebird memory into evidence-backed operating work.
plugins.why: Preserve all thirty methods in their connector-specific pack. Littlebird access and subscription prerequisites are not generic core dependencies.

plugins.name: content-intelligence
plugins.description: Find and verify current repository/news topics and prepare voice-matched drafts.
plugins.why: Keep this small research entry point separate. Its external voice skill and topic ledger must be explicit; do not invent a generic voice asset.

plugins.name: app-primer-zero
plugins.description: Prepare an app library, contracts, schema baseline and a wave handoff before building.
plugins.why: Retain the named new-app journey as a standalone entry point. It reuses core Library/Knowledge/contracts rather than duplicating their agents.

plugins.name: developer-learning-tools
plugins.description: Explain technical sources, prepare beginner builds and teach web fundamentals through bounded projects.
plugins.why: Explain technical sources, prepare beginner builds and teach web fundamentals through bounded projects.

plugins.name: software-economics-tools
plugins.description: Model supplied software economics and costs with explicit scenarios and evidence.
plugins.why: Model supplied software economics and costs with explicit scenarios and evidence.

plugins.name: infrastructure-decision-tools
plugins.description: Prepare platform assets and account dependencies without implicit setup actions.
plugins.why: Prepare platform assets and account dependencies without implicit setup actions.

plugins.name: repository-modernization-tools
plugins.description: Compose repository baseline, safe refactoring and contributor onboarding through selected specialist owners.
plugins.why: Compose repository baseline, safe refactoring and contributor onboarding through selected specialist owners.

plugins.name: product-studio
plugins.description: Turn an idea into a buildable plan: product strategy, Claude-Design-grade UX, a PRD map, a wave plan and a Definition of Done.
plugins.why: Plan before building: owner-approved strategy, UX and build order give Library, contracts and Smoke It one agreed plan.

migration: Fresh installation after purge. No legacy command bridge.
